statements.subject: tcp
statements.description: Implementers MAY include "keep-alives" in their TCP implementations (MAY-5), although this practice is not universally accepted.

statements.subject: user
statements.description: If keep-alives are included, the application MUST be able to turn them on or off for each TCP connection (MUST-24), and they MUST default to off (MUST-25).
actions: allow application to enable or disable keep-alives per TCP connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If keep-alives are included, the application MUST be able to turn them on or off for each TCP connection (MUST-24), and they MUST default to off (MUST-25).
actions: default keep-alive to off for each connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Keep-alive packets MUST only be sent when no sent data is outstanding, and no data or acknowledgment packets have been received for the connection within an interval (MUST-26).

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: This interval MUST be configurable (MUST-27) and MUST default to no less than two hours (MUST-28).

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: This interval MUST be configurable (MUST-27) and MUST default to no less than two hours (MUST-28).
actions: set default keep-alive idle interval to no less than two hours

statements.subject: tcp
statements.description: Consequently, if a keep-alive mechanism is implemented it MUST NOT interpret failure to respond to any specific probe as a dead connection (MUST-29).
statements.pre_cond: keep_alive.implemented = true & keep_alive.probe_sent = true & keep_alive.response_received = false
actions: do not declare connection dead based on failure to respond to any single keep-alive probe

statements.subject: tcp
statements.description: An implementation SHOULD send a keep-alive segment with no data (SHLD-12); however, it MAY be configurable to send a keep-alive segment containing one garbage octet (MAY-6), for compatibility with erroneous TCP implementations.
